content:
I'm not the kind of user who rushes to upgrade every time a new Apple Watch comes out. My current Apple Watch Series 10 only went on sale in September 2024, but I actually only got mine in January this year. Even so, the Apple Watch Series 12 still holds tremendous appeal for me, even though the two share largely the same design language. Here are the reasons I've decided to switch.

That's right, the Series 10 and Series 12 are almost identical in design. You could even say the Series 12 is a slight step backwards, since the bezels are a little thicker. But that's not an issue for me, because the watch face I use has a black background anyway.

That said, the new features of the Apple Watch Series 12 are extremely appealing to me. In particular, the significantly upgraded heart rate monitoring and the all-new "Readiness" app are the main draws. The Series 12 is also noticeably faster in everyday use, and Siri's responsiveness is a prime example of that.

Previous Apple Watches have never fully met my health-tracking needs. The Series 12 is the exact opposite, offering a far richer set of health information. In the past, there were basically just three activity rings and a bunch of data scattered around the Health app. Now, the new Health app presents the information you need to know in a clear and practical way.

I'm still wearing my WHOOP for the time being, mainly because I want to compare the two over an extended period before giving it up entirely, but so far the Apple Health app has performed well, and I'm quite satisfied with the Apple Watch Series 12's health-tracking capabilities.

Top-rated comment published by Nutmac

Michael didn't mention the improvement in battery life, but it's actually quite significant. Based on my daily usage, a single charge easily lasts more than 24 hours.

It's worth noting that WHOOP operates on a subscription model at $239 per year, and compared with the Apple Health app, it no longer has any clear advantage.

Overall, the main reason I bought the Apple Watch Series 12 is that Apple has taken a major step forward in health wearables—the Apple Watch is no longer a product you can take or leave.
